name: Hypertension Assessment Protocol
description: Guided branching triage protocol for ASHA worker hypertension visits. Branches dynamically on symptoms, BP readings, and medication history.

steps.label: Symptom Check
steps.question: Does the patient report dizziness or lightheadedness today?

steps.label: Chest Symptoms
steps.question: Does the patient report any chest pain, tightness, or pressure?

steps.label: Chest Pain — Severity
steps.question: How would the patient describe the chest pain?

steps.label: Respiratory Check
steps.question: Is the patient experiencing difficulty breathing or shortness of breath alongside the chest pain?

steps.label: ⚠ Emergency Action
steps.question: Chest pain with breathing difficulty detected. Has the ASHA worker contacted the PHC emergency line or called for transport?
steps.alert: CRITICAL — Chest pain with breathing difficulty may indicate an acute cardiac event. Call PHC emergency line immediately. Do not leave the patient alone.

steps.label: Clinical Note
steps.question: Chest pain is present but breathing is normal. Has the ASHA worker advised the patient to rest and informed the PHC duty doctor?
steps.alert: ATTENTION — Chest pain present without breathing difficulty. Monitor for worsening. Refer to PHC if symptoms persist beyond 30 minutes.

steps.label: Medication Adherence
steps.question: Has the patient missed any antihypertensive medication in the last 7 days?

steps.label: Adherence — Duration
steps.question: How many days was medication missed?

steps.label: Adherence — Reason
steps.question: What was the primary reason the patient missed their medication?

steps.label: Blood Pressure
steps.question: Record the patient's systolic blood pressure (upper number):

steps.label: Blood Pressure
steps.question: Record the diastolic blood pressure (lower number):

steps.label: ⚠ Hypertensive Crisis
steps.question: BP is severely elevated. Is the patient experiencing severe headache, blurred vision, nausea, or confusion?
steps.alert: HYPERTENSIVE CRISIS — Systolic ≥ 180 or Diastolic ≥ 110. Immediate hospital referral required. Do not send home.

steps.label: Crisis — Referral
steps.question: Has the patient been referred to the nearest district hospital or PHC for immediate management?

steps.label: ⚠ Escalation Required
steps.question: Patient has refused or transport is unavailable. Has the ASHA supervisor or block health officer been notified?
steps.alert: Document refusal in writing. Notify supervisor immediately. Follow PHC escalation protocol.

steps.label: Elevated BP
steps.question: BP is elevated (≥ 160 mmHg). Is the patient also experiencing dizziness alongside this elevated reading?
steps.alert: Elevated BP — Stage 2 Hypertension. Reinforce medication adherence. Schedule follow-up within 7 days.

steps.label: Dizziness + High BP
steps.question: Dizziness with elevated BP may indicate hypertensive urgency. Has the patient been physically exerted or under significant stress recently?

steps.label: Clinical Notes
steps.question: Any additional clinical observations or follow-up actions to note?
